## Question

Polls put Peter Obi first; he finished third. At 2,000 interviews the margin is ±2.18 points (proof). The miss was 19.29 points (proof). Was the sample too small?

## Claim

On TVC, three weeks before the vote, El-Rufai [dismissed the polls](https://guardian.ng/news/el-rufai-debunks-obis-election-win-predictions-calls-opinion-polls-a-joke/):

<figure class="portrait-inline">
<img src="el-rufai-2023.jpg" alt="Nasir el-Rufai in a brown hat and dark glasses, mid-gesture, in February 2023.">
<figcaption>VOA / Wikimedia Commons, public domain</figcaption>
</figure>

> Opinion polls are distorted... When you have about a 100 million registered voters and you are
> sampling 2,000 registered voters or 300 registered voters, your results from day one are
> unreliable; they will have high margins of error.

He was right that they were wrong.

## Counter-claim

His next sentence is the better objection.

> Most of these polls, like the one by Bloomberg, ANAP and the one by Okonjo Iweala, all used
> telephone. What percentage of registered voters have phone numbers in INEC's records? We have
> found out and it's 31 per cent.

Only 31 per cent of the register can be telephoned (assume). The simulation prices it. Five hundred, whole register: winner right 3,967 of 4,000 (sim). Forty thousand, phones: winner right 0 of 4,000 (sim).

## Setup

NaijaSim is invented: 90,000,000 voters, six zones, four colour-named parties (assume). Phone reach is his 31 per cent (assume). The truth is fixed before anyone is interviewed.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false
library(plotly)

comma <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", big.mark = ",", digits = digits)
}

z <- qnorm(0.975)                        # 95% two-sided

# The post's palette: one hue per stream already exists; these four are the
# parties, and ink is the truth line rather than a party.
pal  <- c("#0f766e", "#0e7490", "#b45309", "#6d28d9")
ink  <- "#57606a"
grid <- "#d7dce1"
```

```{r}
#| label: inputs
#| output: false
# ---- Quoted inputs. Every other number in this post derives from these. ----

# ANAP Foundation / NOIPolls, February 2023; see the method note below.
anap_n <- 2000
poll <- c(Obi = 21, Tinubu = 13, Atiku = 10, Kwankwaso = 3,
          Undecided = 23, Refused = 30)

elrufai_n   <- 40000    # his own poll, as he described it on air
phone_share <- 0.31     # his figure for phone coverage, not checked against INEC

# INEC, 2023 presidential election.
registered  <- 93469008
votes_cast  <- 24965218
votes_valid <- 24025940
votes <- c(Obi = 6101533, Tinubu = 8794726,
           Atiku = 6984520, Kwankwaso = 1496687)

# A mistyped input should fail the render rather than publish quietly.
stopifnot(
  sum(poll) == 100,
  sum(votes) <= votes_valid,
  votes_valid <= votes_cast,
  votes_cast <= registered
)
```

```{r}
#| label: shares
#| output: false
# Fifty-three of every hundred respondents were undecided or would not say, so the
# headline numbers do not sum to anything like a vote share. Comparing with the
# result means rebasing onto the respondents who named a candidate.
decided  <- sum(poll[names(votes)])
poll_obi <- poll[["Obi"]] / decided
act_obi  <- votes[["Obi"]] / votes_valid
miss     <- poll_obi - act_obi
```

```{r}
#| label: correction
#| output: false
fpc     <- sqrt((registered - anap_n) / (registered - 1))
se_anap <- sqrt(poll_obi * (1 - poll_obi) / anap_n)
```

```{r}
#| label: distance
#| output: false
# The sample size at which the margin of error would have been as wide as the
# miss, i.e. the only n for which the objection lands.
n_cross <- ceiling(z^2 * poll_obi * (1 - poll_obi) / miss^2)
```

## The simulation

```{r}
#| label: naijasim
#| message: false
#| output: false
set.seed(20260817)

sim_party <- c("Green", "Blue", "Red", "Yellow")
sim_zone  <- c("North West", "North East", "North Central",
               "South West", "South East", "South South")
sim_reg_z <- c(21, 12, 15, 18, 9, 15) * 1e6      # registered voters, by zone
names(sim_reg_z) <- sim_zone

# The national result, set by fiat. Blue wins.
sim_target <- c(Green = 0.30, Blue = 0.38, Red = 0.24, Yellow = 0.08)

# Zone shares are chosen, EXCEPT North Central, solved so the register-weighted
# truth lands exactly on sim_target.
sim_zs <- rbind(
  c(0.08, 0.50, 0.36, 0.06),
  c(0.10, 0.52, 0.32, 0.06),
  c(NA,   NA,   NA,   NA  ),
  c(0.34, 0.34, 0.22, 0.10),
  c(0.72, 0.12, 0.08, 0.08),
  c(0.48, 0.26, 0.16, 0.10)
)
dimnames(sim_zs) <- list(sim_zone, sim_party)
i_nc <- match("North Central", sim_zone)
sim_zs[i_nc, ] <- (sum(sim_reg_z) * sim_target -
                   colSums(sim_zs[-i_nc, ] * sim_reg_z[-i_nc])) / sim_reg_z[i_nc]

# Phone reach is chosen, EXCEPT South South, solved so national coverage is
# exactly the 31 per cent he quoted. The poorest zones reach fewest.
sim_reach_z <- c(`North West` = 0.160, `North East` = 0.120,
                 `North Central` = 0.300, `South West` = 0.500,
                 `South East` = 0.440, `South South` = NA)[sim_zone]
i_ss <- match("South South", sim_zone)
sim_reach_z[i_ss] <- (phone_share * sum(sim_reg_z) -
                      sum((sim_reg_z * sim_reach_z)[-i_ss])) / sim_reg_z[i_ss]

# Each zone splits 60/40 into two states leaning opposite ways, so no stratum is
# internally uniform. B moves 1.5x as far as A, preserving the zone average; the
# 0.5 cap keeps every state inside (0, 1).
sim_st <- NULL; sim_reg_s <- numeric(0); sim_szone <- character(0)
for (zn in sim_zone) {
  g <- sim_zs[zn, "Green"]; b <- sim_zs[zn, "Blue"]
  d <- 0.5 * min(g / 1.5, b)
  s_a <- sim_zs[zn, ]; s_a["Green"] <- g + d;       s_a["Blue"] <- b - d
  s_b <- sim_zs[zn, ]; s_b["Green"] <- g - 1.5 * d; s_b["Blue"] <- b + 1.5 * d
  sim_st    <- rbind(sim_st, s_a, s_b)
  sim_reg_s <- c(sim_reg_s, 0.60 * sim_reg_z[[zn]], 0.40 * sim_reg_z[[zn]])
  sim_szone <- c(sim_szone, zn, zn)
}
sim_frame_s <- sim_reg_s * unname(sim_reach_z[sim_szone])

# A mistyped country should fail the render rather than publish quietly.
stopifnot(
  sum(sim_reg_z) == 90e6,
  all(abs(rowSums(sim_st) - 1) < 1e-12),
  all(sim_st > 0), all(sim_st < 1),
  isTRUE(all.equal(colSums(sim_st * sim_reg_s) / sum(sim_reg_s), sim_target)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(sum(sim_frame_s) / sum(sim_reg_s), phone_share))
)

sim_w_true  <- sim_reg_s   / sum(sim_reg_s)     # a fair poll's weights
sim_w_frame <- sim_frame_s / sum(sim_frame_s)   # what a phone poll actually gets
sim_truth   <- colSums(sim_st * sim_w_true)
sim_ptruth  <- colSums(sim_st * sim_w_frame)
sim_frame_N <- sum(sim_frame_s)
```

```{r}
#| label: naijasim-runs
#| output: false
# Seeded here, not left to the chunk above, so these numbers do not depend on
# how many draws the country construction happened to consume.
set.seed(20260817)

# Largest remainder: proportional shares rounded the obvious way do not sum to n.
sim_alloc <- function(n, w) {
  raw <- n * w; a <- floor(raw); k <- n - sum(a)
  if (k > 0) { j <- order(raw - a, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(k)]; a[j] <- a[j] + 1 }
  stopifnot(sum(a) == n)
  a
}

SIM_REPS <- 4000

# One rmultinom call per state, vectorised over all 4,000 repetitions.
sim_run <- function(n, w) {
  a <- sim_alloc(n, w)
  est <- matrix(0, SIM_REPS, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, sim_party))
  for (i in seq_along(a)) {
    if (a[i] == 0) next
    est <- est + w[i] * t(rmultinom(SIM_REPS, a[i], sim_st[i, ])) / a[i]
  }
  est
}

# "Right" means Blue tops the poll, not merely Blue ahead of Green.
sim_summ <- function(est) {
  g <- 100 * est[, "Green"]
  c(green = mean(g), sd = sd(g),
    right = 100 * mean(sim_party[max.col(est, ties.method = "first")] == "Blue"))
}

sim_ns_fair  <- c(n_cross, 100, 250, 500, 1000, anap_n)
sim_ns_phone <- c(anap_n, elrufai_n)
sim_fair  <- lapply(sim_ns_fair,  sim_run, w = sim_w_true)
sim_phone <- lapply(sim_ns_phone, sim_run, w = sim_w_frame)
sim_ft    <- t(sapply(sim_fair,  sim_summ))
sim_pt    <- t(sapply(sim_phone, sim_summ))

# Indexed by value, not position, so the prose survives a reordered ladder.
i_win <- match(500, sim_ns_fair)     # the rung the argument turns on
i_2k  <- match(anap_n, sim_ns_fair)
j_2k  <- match(anap_n, sim_ns_phone)
j_40k <- match(elrufai_n, sim_ns_phone)
```

### What a phone frame actually is

Through a phone, Green leads by 3.5 points (sim). In the country, Blue leads by 8 (sim). The figure is not a smaller copy of the country; it is a different country, one that leans Green. Each coloured box is one party's share. The two groups are the two frames. They are the invented country's truth, not Nigeria's result.

```{r}
#| label: fig-country
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "A phone frame is a different country, leaning Green."

c1 <- data.frame(
  party = factor(rep(sim_party, 2), levels = sim_party),
  where = rep(c("whole register", "phone frame"), each = length(sim_party)),
  share = 100 * c(sim_truth[sim_party], sim_ptruth[sim_party])
)

# Each bar is a party, coloured by its own name, so no legend has to be
# decoded. The two frames are the two groups on the x-axis.
pal_party <- c("#15803d", "#1e40af", "#b91c1c", "#a16207")

fig_c1 <- plot_ly(data = c1, height = 380,
  x = ~where, y = ~share, color = ~party, colors = pal_party,
  type = "bar", text = ~sprintf("%.1f", share), textposition = "outside",
  textfont = list(size = 14, color = ink),
  hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.1f}%<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>")

fig_c1 <- layout(fig_c1,
  # bargap only: plotly's R layout has no bargroupgap, and an unknown attribute
  # prints a warning into the body of the page rather than being ignored.
  barmode = "group", bargap = 0.35,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 20, t = 55, b = 10),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, xanchor = "left", y = 1.2,
    yanchor = "top", font = list(size = 13)),
  shapes = list(
    list(type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
      y0 = 100 * sim_truth[["Green"]], y1 = 100 * sim_truth[["Green"]],
      line = list(color = "#15803d", width = 1, dash = "dot")),
    list(type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
      y0 = 100 * sim_truth[["Blue"]], y1 = 100 * sim_truth[["Blue"]],
      line = list(color = "#1e40af", width = 1, dash = "dot"))),
  xaxis = list(title = "", tickfont = list(size = 15)),
  yaxis = list(title = "share of the vote (%)", range = c(0, 54),
    gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 13)),
  annotations = list(
    list(x = "whole register", y = 50, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "center", font = list(size = 13, color = "#1e40af"),
      text = sprintf("Blue +%.0f",
        100 * (sim_truth[["Blue"]] - sim_truth[["Green"]]))),
    list(x = "phone frame", y = 50, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "center", font = list(size = 13, color = "#15803d"),
      text = sprintf("Green +%.1f",
        100 * (sim_ptruth[["Green"]] - sim_ptruth[["Blue"]])))))
config(fig_c1, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: each bar is a party, coloured by its name; the phone frame lifts Green and cuts Blue, while the dotted lines mark the country's true shares.*

### The spoon, priced: population size buys nothing

Population size is worth 0.0011% of the margin (proof). That is his objection, priced.

```{r}
#| label: fig-spoon-price
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Ninety million voters buy 0.0011% of the margin."

c2_n <- sort(unique(c(round(exp(seq(log(26), log(40000), length.out = 80))),
                      26, 500, 2000, 40000)))
c2 <- data.frame(n = c2_n)
c2$plain <- 100 * z * sqrt(poll_obi * (1 - poll_obi) / c2$n)
c2$fpc   <- c2$plain * sqrt((registered - c2$n) / (registered - 1))

fig_c2 <- plot_ly(data = c2, x = ~n, y = ~plain, type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
  name = "population ignored", line = list(color = "#0e7490", width = 3),
  hovertemplate = "%{x:,.0f}: ±%{y:.2f}<extra></extra>")
# Drawn second, dashed, on top of the first. The gap between them is the whole
# population correction, and at any real sample size it is thinner than a pixel:
# the dashes riding the solid line ARE the finding.
fig_c2 <- add_trace(fig_c2, data = c2, x = ~n, y = ~fpc, mode = "lines",
  name = "population known",
  line = list(color = "#b45309", width = 2, dash = "dot"),
  fill = "tonexty", fillcolor = "rgba(180, 83, 9, 0.35)", hoverinfo = "skip")
fig_c2 <- layout(fig_c2,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 20, t = 50, b = 10),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.18, font = list(size = 12)),
  xaxis = list(title = "interviews (log scale)", type = "log",
    range = c(log10(20), log10(60000)),
    tickvals = c(26, 100, 500, 2000, 10000, 40000),
    ticktext = c("26", "100", "500", "2,000", "10,000", "40,000"),
    tickfont = list(size = 13), gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE),
  yaxis = list(title = "95% margin of error (points)", range = c(0, 24),
    gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 13)),
  shapes = list(
    list(type = "line", x0 = anap_n, x1 = anap_n,
      y0 = 0, y1 = 100 * z * se_anap,
      line = list(color = ink, width = 1, dash = "dot")),
    list(type = "line", x0 = elrufai_n, x1 = elrufai_n,
      y0 = 0, y1 = 24,
      line = list(color = "#6b7280", width = 1, dash = "dot")),
    list(type = "line", x0 = 20, x1 = 60000,
      y0 = 100 * miss, y1 = 100 * miss,
      line = list(color = "#b45309", width = 1.5, dash = "dash"))),
  annotations = list(
    list(x = anap_n, y = 3.8, xanchor = "right",
      text = sprintf("%s interviews: ±%.2f", comma(anap_n), 100 * z * se_anap),
      showarrow = TRUE, ax = 0, ay = 30, font = list(size = 13, color = ink)),
    list(x = 26, y = 21.6, xanchor = "left", showarrow = FALSE,
      text = "the two lines are one line",
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#b45309")),
    list(x = elrufai_n, y = 22.5, xanchor = "right", showarrow = FALSE,
      text = "his poll: 40,000",
      font = list(size = 12, color = "#6b7280")),
    list(x = 2000, y = 100 * miss + 0.6, xanchor = "left", showarrow = FALSE,
      text = sprintf("the actual miss: %.2f pts", 100 * miss),
      font = list(size = 12, color = "#b45309"))))
config(fig_c2, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: the two lines are one line; the shaded sliver is the entire population correction.*

### Four thousand runs: sample size is not the fix

Five hundred beats forty thousand, eighty times smaller (sim). The frame never climbs. The ladder: Blue tops 4,000 polls 64% of the time at 500 interviews and 100% at 2,000; never, even at 40,000, on the phone frame. The trend is precision, not accuracy. More interviews sharpen a fair poll toward 100 (sim). The phone line never leaves zero (sim).

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Bigger spoon, same corner. The frame never wins."

c3 <- data.frame(
  n     = c(sim_ns_fair, sim_ns_phone),
  # sim_ft / sim_pt already hold percentages, so these are not scaled again.
  right = c(sim_ft[, "right"], sim_pt[, "right"]),
  where = rep(c("whole register", "phone frame"),
              c(length(sim_ns_fair), length(sim_ns_phone)))
)
on_register <- c3$where == "whole register"

rung <- function(fig, d, col, nm) {
  add_trace(fig, data = d, x = ~n, y = ~right, type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines+markers+text", name = nm,
    line = list(color = col, width = 2.5),
    marker = list(color = col, size = 10),
    text = ~sprintf("%.1f", right), textposition = "top center",
    textfont = list(size = 12, color = ink),
    hovertemplate = paste0("%{x:,.0f}: %{y:.1f}%<extra>", nm, "</extra>"))
}

fig_c3 <- plot_ly(height = 400)
fig_c3 <- rung(fig_c3, c3[on_register, ], "#0f766e", "whole register")
fig_c3 <- rung(fig_c3, c3[!on_register, ], "#b45309", "phone frame")
fig_c3 <- layout(fig_c3,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 95, t = 30, b = 10),
  shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = 18, x1 = 90000,
    y0 = 100, y1 = 100,
    line = list(color = ink, width = 1, dash = "dot"))),
  showlegend = FALSE,
  xaxis = list(title = "interviews (log scale)", type = "log",
    range = c(log10(18), log10(90000)),
    tickvals = c(26, 100, 500, 2000, 10000, 40000),
    ticktext = c("26", "100", "500", "2,000", "10,000", "40,000"),
    tickfont = list(size = 13), gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE),
  yaxis = list(title = "winner named right (% of 4,000 runs)",
    range = c(-8, 112), gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE,
    tickfont = list(size = 13)),
  annotations = list(
    list(xref = "paper", x = 1.01, y = 100, text = "whole register",
      showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left",
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#0f766e")),
    list(xref = "paper", x = 1.01, y = 0, text = "phone frame",
      showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left",
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#b45309")),
    list(x = 7000, y = 16, xanchor = "right", text = "40,000 interviews, still 0",
      showarrow = TRUE, ax = 26, ay = -14,
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#b45309")),
    list(xref = "paper", x = 1.02, y = 100, text = "truth: Blue wins",
      showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left",
      font = list(size = 11, color = ink))))
config(fig_c3, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: one line climbs, the other flatlines at zero — the gap is the frame.*

### The same answer, harder: precision without accuracy

At 2,000, phones wobble 0.96 points against 0.87 fair (sim). Narrowest, and furthest from the truth.

```{r}
#| label: fig-density
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Narrow, and furthest from the truth."

# ~80 points per curve, binned here; the 4,000 raw draws would ship the whole
# simulation to the browser. See CLAUDE.md on page weight.
sim_curve <- function(e) {
  d <- density(100 * e[, "Green"], n = 80)
  data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y / max(d$y))
}

c4 <- list(
  sim_curve(sim_fair[[i_win]]), sim_curve(sim_fair[[i_2k]]),
  sim_curve(sim_phone[[j_2k]]), sim_curve(sim_phone[[j_40k]])
)
c4_lab <- c(paste0("register, ", comma(sim_ns_fair[i_win])),
            paste0("register, ", comma(anap_n)),
            paste0("phone, ", comma(anap_n)),
            paste0("phone, ", comma(elrufai_n)))

fig_c4 <- plot_ly(height = 410)
for (i in seq_along(c4)) {
  fig_c4 <- add_trace(fig_c4, data = c4[[i]], x = ~x, y = ~y, type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines", name = c4_lab[i], fill = "tozeroy",
    line = list(color = pal[i], width = 2.5),
    fillcolor = paste0(pal[i], "33"), hoverinfo = "skip")
}

# Direct labels at each peak instead of a four-item legend. Two curves sit close
# together on each side, so a label that would land within 4.5 points of its
# neighbour's is lifted a step — otherwise the two register curves print over
# each other and each one's colour is the only thing telling them apart.
c4_pk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(c4), function(i) {
  d <- c4[[i]]
  data.frame(lab = c4_lab[i], col = pal[i], x = d$x[which.max(d$y)], y = 1.04,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
c4_pk <- c4_pk[order(c4_pk$x), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(c4_pk))) {
  if (i > 1 && abs(c4_pk$x[i] - c4_pk$x[i - 1]) < 4.5) {
    c4_pk$y[i] <- c4_pk$y[i - 1] + 0.16
  }
}
c4_ann <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(c4_pk)), function(i) list(
  x = c4_pk$x[i], y = c4_pk$y[i], text = c4_pk$lab[i], showarrow = FALSE,
  xanchor = "center", yanchor = "bottom",
  font = list(size = 12, color = c4_pk$col[i])))

# The truth, as a rule: a trace, not a layout shape, because shape and
# annotation coordinates disagree on some axis types.
fig_c4 <- add_trace(fig_c4, x = rep(100 * sim_truth[["Green"]], 2),
  y = c(0, 1.08), type = "scatter", mode = "lines", showlegend = FALSE,
  line = list(color = ink, width = 1.2, dash = "dot"), hoverinfo = "skip")
fig_c4 <- add_trace(fig_c4, x = rep(100 * sim_ptruth[["Green"]], 2),
  y = c(0, 1.08), type = "scatter", mode = "lines", showlegend = FALSE,
  line = list(color = "#6b7280", width = 1.2, dash = "dash"), hoverinfo = "skip")

fig_c4 <- layout(fig_c4,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 10, t = 30, b = 10),
  showlegend = FALSE,
  xaxis = list(title = "what the poll says Green got (%)",
    range = range(unlist(lapply(c4, `[[`, "x"))) + c(-0.5, 0.5),
    zeroline = FALSE, gridcolor = grid, tickfont = list(size = 13)),
  yaxis = list(showticklabels = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE,
    range = c(0, 1.5), title = ""),
  annotations = c(c4_ann, list(
    list(x = 100 * sim_truth[["Green"]], y = 1.4, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "center", font = list(size = 12, color = ink),
      text = sprintf("register truth: %.1f%%", 100 * sim_truth[["Green"]])),
    list(x = 100 * sim_ptruth[["Green"]], y = 1.45, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "center", font = list(size = 11, color = "#6b7280"),
      text = sprintf("phone truth: %.1f%%", 100 * sim_ptruth[["Green"]])),
    list(x = c4_pk$x[c4_pk$lab == c4_lab[4]], y = 0.62, xanchor = "right",
      text = "narrowest, and furthest from the truth",
      showarrow = TRUE, ax = -30, ay = 30,
      font = list(size = 12, color = pal[4])))))
config(fig_c4, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: four bell curves, narrowest on the right; the truth lines mark each frame's centre.*

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Where the numbers come from

**The margin.** For a proportion $p$ from $n$ draws, $SE=\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}$. Population size enters
only through the finite population correction $\sqrt{(N-n)/(N-1)}$, which at
$n=2{,}000$ against $N=93{,}469{,}008$ is `r sprintf("%.7f", fpc)` — a shrinkage of
`r sprintf("%.4f%%", 100 * (1 - fpc))` of the standard error.

**The miss.** Obi polled `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * poll_obi)` of decided respondents and took
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * act_obi)` of valid votes: a gap of `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * miss)`
points, or `r sprintf("%.1f", miss / se_anap)` standard errors. Inverting the margin for the sample
size that would cover a miss that large gives `r comma(n_cross)` interviews — the rung on the left
of the ladder, and the reason the ladder starts there.

**The country.** NaijaSim is invented and deliberately not a model of Nigeria. Zone names are real;
register, zone splits, parties and result are made up, because verifiable zone-level 2023 figures do
not exist from one authoritative source and inventing them while calling them the past would be
worse than inventing a country and saying so. Ninety million registered, six zones, four
colour-named parties, and coverage of `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * phone_share)` borrowed from his own
figure. Seeded at 20260817; 4,000 repetitions at each sample size; stratified by state.

**Quoted, not derived.** The El-Rufai quotations are as reported by
[The Guardian Nigeria](https://guardian.ng/news/el-rufai-debunks-obis-election-win-predictions-calls-opinion-polls-a-joke/)
from *Journalists' Hangout* on TVC News, 4 February 2023. The sample size, phone-based stratified
random method and the six percentages come from
[ANAP Foundation's press release](https://www.anapfoundation.com/press-releases/2023-elections-peter-obi-maintains-lead-amongst-presidential-poll-respondents);
the register and valid votes are INEC's, via the
[published breakdown](https://dailypost.ng/2023/03/01/2023-elections-breakdown-of-results-as-tinubu-defeats-atiku-obi/).
Outlets differ on the second figure in that first quotation, The Guardian having "300" where
[The Cable](https://www.thecable.ng/noi-poll-weve-been-using-same-methodology-since-2015-anap-foundation-replies-critics/)
reports "three thousand"; the arithmetic uses ANAP's published `r comma(anap_n)`, so nothing turns
on it. His own `r comma(elrufai_n)`-sample poll has no published methodology I could find, and
appears here as a sample size and nothing else.

**The portrait.** `File:Nasir Ahmed el-Rufai 2023.jpg` on Wikimedia Commons, 470 × 662, tagged
PD-VOA: a Voice of America work, so public domain in the United States rather than openly licensed.
The Commons page records it as a VOA Africa upload, which is what makes the tag stick.

**Attribution, split deliberately.** That accuracy depends on absolute sample size rather than on
the sampling fraction is standard, and Freedman, Pisani and Purves develop it in the chapter on
chance errors in sampling in *Statistics*. The soup-and-spoon comparison is attributed to
[George Gallup](https://nrich.maths.org/13895), not to them, because I could not verify that the
book uses the soup wording.
:::

::: {.aside-box .hommie}
> So five hundred people told you who won, and forty thousand did not?

He was half right. The phone polls were wrong, and the simulation agrees every run. But sample size was not why. Forty thousand phone interviews named the winner 0 times in 4,000 (sim). Five hundred from the whole register named it 3,967 times (sim). The spoon was never too small. It never reached the bottom.
:::
